rationale:
Evidence: the only design with a verified score is the raced iteration-7 design, which scored 344.4979. Iterations 8 and 9 reproduced that score to four decimals on all 60 trials, so the race is deterministic and the record is trustworthy. The outcome table records that design as kd 0.35, ki 0.5, kp 2.0, base_speed 1.5, line_loss 'last_direction'. The authorized entity1 text describes kd 0.25 and 'search_left', which never raced and conflicts with the scored record. I therefore keep the scored record, not the entity1 text. Its oval completion is 17 of 20 (mean progress 0.95, mean time 1.86 s). Its s-bend (progress 0.34, 1.15 line-loss events) and slalom (progress 0.11, 1.25 line-loss events) both still leave the tape.

Critique points accepted: the draft's altered plant (body 0.12, mass 0.6, wheel_track 0.10, sensors at y 0.06) was never raced, so I restore the verified geometry exactly. kd is not a tuning lever in this range (0.25 and 0.35 and 0.4 gave identical results), so I keep kd 0.35 as raced. The round-2 critique's point that the record should be the baseline is also accepted.

Critique points partly accepted: speed is the one lever not yet tested on the verified plant, and the s-bend and slalom failures are spatial, so a slower entry may give more correction time. I test base_speed 1.5 to 1.3 as the only change. The critique warns that lower base PWM raises effective steering gain, so steering_oscillation may rise, and that the oval time rises from about 1.86 s toward about 2.15 s, still under 3.0 s. I accept that risk because this is a test on an iteration that is followed by one more iteration, and reverting is cheap.

Change from the scored record: base_speed 1.5 to 1.3, nothing else.

Expected result: oval completion stays at 15 to 17 of 20, and s-bend progress rises above 0.335. I expect steering_oscillation on the oval to rise modestly from 0.197, because of the higher effective gain. Falsification: oval completions below 15 of 20, or a total score below 344.5, rejects the speed hypothesis, and base_speed returns to 1.5 for the final design. A mixed result (oval unchanged, s-bend progress up slightly) is treated as inconclusive, and I would not change the final design on it alone. An identical score would indicate the change did not reach the race.
